patch.lastPrompt: You are an expert C++ to Rust migration engineer. Read the following C++ source code: --- Source (/[redacted].cpp) --- #include "../sortedcontainers.h" #include <iostream> int main(int argc, char* argv[]) { int n = 6; if (argc > 1) { n = std::atoi(argv[1]); } SortedSet<int> s1, s2; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { s1.insert(i); s2.insert(i*2); } auto s3 = s1.union_with(s2); std::cout << s1.size() << std::endl; std::cout << s2.size() << std::endl; std::cout << s3.size() << std::endl; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { std::cout << s3.contains(i) << " "; } std::cout << std::endl; return 0; } /* ============================== TEST CASE EXAMPLES (Top 5) ============================== --- Example 1 --- Input Args: {"n": "0"} Program Output: 0 0 0 --- Example 2 --- Input Args: {"n": "1"} Program Output: 1 1 1 1 --- Example 3 --- Input Args: {"n": "2"} Program Output: 2 2 3 1 1 --- Example 4 --- Input Args: {"n": "3"} Program Output: 3 3 4 1 1 1 --- Example 5 --- Input Args: {"n": "4"} Program Output: 4 4 6 1 1 1 1 */ --- Requirements: 1. **Environment**: Write pure Rust using the 2021 edition. Code must compile with `rustc` or as a Cargo project. 2. **CLI arguments**: The Rust binary must accept exactly the same command-line arguments as the C++ binary (same names, defaults, and required fields). Parse args via `std::env::args()`. 3. **Logic and output**: Algorithm logic, numeric precision, and string formatting must exactly match the C++ source. `println!` output must be byte-for-byte identical to `std::cout` output. 4. **Zero external dependencies**: Do NOT use any crates from crates.io (only `std`). Forbidden crates for this repo: none. Implement all functionality from scratch using the standard library. 5. **Project structure**: Create a complete Cargo project in `/output`. Organize library code into modules. Place the entry test file `test6.rs` in the package root `/output`. 6. **Black-box implementation**: Do not read the C++ library source. Infer behavior from the interface, then re-implement using `std`. 7. **Output**: - Create and implement library files inside `/output`. - Save the entry file to `/output/test6.rs`. - Compile and produce an executable at `/output/test6.rs` (by running `rustc test6.rs` or `cargo build --release`). Hint: `/workspace/dataset/test6_executable` is the compiled C++ binary — use it to debug with any arguments.

args.command: cd /output && rustc --edition 2021 -O test6.rs -o test6 && echo BUILD_OK

args.command:
cd /output && for args in "" "0" "1" "2" "3" "4" "6" "10" "-3" "abc" "  +7xyz"; do
  ref=$(/workspace/dataset/test6_executable $args | od -c | head -20)
  mine=$(./test6 $args | od -c | head -20)
  if [ "$ref" = "$mine" ]; then echo "OK   args=[$args]"; else echo "DIFF args=[$args]"; fi
done
